- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +1.3 to -1.2), model lags in correction; add 1–2 days of downward adjustment to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is bullish and price has been trending up for 5+ days.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.5–1.0 alternating), model tends to oscillate; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values unless sentiment is clearly trending.
